For a conclusion at order $n$, the formal statement needs the weighted coefficient bounds (D.7) only for $1\le m\le n$. It then proves $\|v\|_{[n]}\le C_nC_{m low}\|f\|_{[n]}$, preserving one factor of the zero-order bound. The spaces are arbitrary real seminormed vector spaces and the derivatives form an arbitrary finite ordered family. Thus constraints, equations modulo gradients and prescribed data must be represented in the chosen solution and forcing spaces and their derivative maps. The weighted spatial-and-phase norms, or the half-Hölder norms, are applications after these choices. The constant is selected before the spaces, maps and coefficients, but may depend on the number of derivative directions, which is fixed in the paper. It does not depend on the values of the derivative maps: those are introduced after the constant. The result estimates existing solutions; it asserts no existence or invertibility of a general equation.
